articles.title: Captain Price Actor Sends Message to Fans as Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Campaign Praise Rolls in
articles.summary: Barry Sloane, the actor behind Call of Duty's Captain Price, has shared a message with fans as praise for Modern Warfare 4's campaign rolls in. Early reactions to Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's story mode have filled social media feeds in the first 24 hours since early access players dived in …
body: It appears to be a winner for publisher Activision and developer Infinity Ward that critics like, too. While Steam reviews paint a "Very Positive" picture, IGN awarded this year's set of story missions an 8/10. Our reviewer said the Modern Warfare 4 campaign made them "feel something for the series again," adding that it managed to send the reboot saga series out "on a high note."
"The MW4 campaign was a 10/10 for me, they made a good story and ended it," one recent Steam review said. "Damn near almost cried at the end LOL."

As reviews continue to trickle in, many have taken the time to praise Sloane's work as Captain Price, specifically. The star behind Activision's most recent incarnation of the Task Force 141 leader took to social media to respond to the "kind words" he's received.
"Thank you for all the kind words," he said. "I see them. I read them. And I am grateful."

body: Dungeons & Dragons: World of Warcraft is less than a month away, and it already looks like it's going to be a massive expansion to the tabletop game. articles.title: The 8 Best Castlevania Games, Ranked
articles.summary: Castlevania is one of the most beloved franchises in video game history, despite a period of 13 years when we didn’t see a new installment until the launch of Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse earlier this week.
body: Over the years, the games have provided a variety of experiences, mixed with rich lore built on the vampire myth. With so many games available to choose from, it can be difficult to know where to begin if you haven’t touched the series in a while. Accordingly, here is our ranked list of the 8 best Castlevania games. It should make an excellent starting point.
A weekly cheat sheet to what you’ll eventually love to play. No buying, no commitment — just saving for later.

Check our full Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse review for all the details, but the short version is this: you need to play the game. It respects the series’ history while mapping out a potential future we hope the developers will one day realize with follow-up titles. The 2.5D visuals give each area a new sense of depth, while enabling the satisfying Metroidvania mechanics players have enjoyed since Symphony of the Night changed the franchise forever. Fluid movement during combat, a killer soundtrack to match the moonlit ambience of the visuals, and a brave new hero all add up to one of the very finest entries the series has ever seen.

articles.title: True Detective Season 5 to feature the best starring duo since Matthew McConaughey and Woody Harrelson
articles.summary: True Detective fans just got some exciting news: two of the main cast members and the setting of the show's fifth season have been revealed. The casting announcements are especially exciting, as it has been confirmed that Nicolas Cage and Antonio Banderas will star as the headlining duo in Season 5.
body: True Detective has garnered a reputation as one of the best and most influential crime dramas on television, with its influence most recently being felt in DC Studios' Lanterns. Each season follows a different pair of detectives as they unravel high-stakes mysteries across the United States. The last season aired in 2024 and starred Jodie Foster and Kali Reis, but the first season, featuring Matthew McConaughey and Woody Harrelson, remains the most iconic.

If any pair of actors can challenge McConaughey and Harrelson for the True Detective crown, it'll be Nicolas Cage and Antonio Banderas. Variety reports that Cage's character is named Henry Logan, while Banderas will portray Rai García. We don't know much more about those characters, but it's safe to assume they'll be the detectives that the fifth season focuses on.

That report also confirms the season will be set in Jamaica Bay, which is part of Long Island in New York. We also know that production will begin in 2027 and that Season 4 showrunner Issa López will return to write, direct, and executive produce the fifth season.
points: True Detective fans just got some exciting news: two of the main cast members and the setting of the show's fifth season have been revealed.

articles.title: 7 Crazy Movie Premises That Actually Worked
articles.summary: Before Whalefall, these crazy movie premises actually worked too.
body: “A young man is swallowed by a whale while searching for his father’s remains deep in the ocean.”

That is the elevator pitch for Whalefall, starring Austin Abrams (Resident Evil) and co-written by Daniel Kraus and director Brian Duffield (No One Will Save You). Set for release on October 16, the film is based on Kraus’ 2023 novel, inspired by a viral video of kayakers seemingly being swallowed by a whale. Whalefall’s central conceit is one writers and directors are challenged by, and often dream of, because it raises the questions: Can I pull this off? And how can I make this work? In other words, the absolutely bonkers premise is fertile ground for real creative risk and opportunity.

articles.title: US Representative Introduces Plan To Preserve Digital Game Ownership
articles.summary: United States Representative Ritchie Torres will introduce the Power To The Players Act. This legislation is being made to support consumers' rights in a way that grants gamers ownership of their digital games.
body: Some companies are trying to preserve physical media and keep the disc format alive, but physical games are now endangered. With several publishers no longer selling physical versions, Sony ending disc production, and uncertainty around Project Helix's disc drive, the gaming world is headed towards an all-digital future, and gamers aren't happy.

Regardless of what the future holds for physical games, digital media currently dominates the gaming market. That is why Rep. Ritchie Torres wants to cement gamers' ownership rights over their digital libraries with the introduction of the Power To The Players bill.

At the moment, companies have full control of gamers' digital licenses. Digital storefronts can delist games, cutting off access to a wide audience within seconds. Developers can shut down servers if a game isn't as profitable as they had hoped, stripping gamers of online features promised on launch. As Torres puts it, families use their savings to purchase games, but with a digital license, the software that they paid for can be "pulled out from under them on a company's arbitrary timeline."
points: United States Representative Ritchie Torres will introduce the Power To The Players Act.

articles.title: 22 Years Ago, One Perfect Twist Changed TV's Greatest Sci-Fi Series Forever
articles.summary: At the time, Lindelof was discussing his new series, Lost — which just four episodes in, had pulled off a mind-blowing twist arguably on the same level as The Sixth Sense. For its first few episodes, Lost seems like an ambitious survival drama with a dash of horror.
body: The best twists totally recontextualize everything that’s come before them. Mystery-box series master Damon Lindelof ( Lanterns, Watchmen ) once cited The Sixth Sense as the definitive example: The movie works if Bruce Willis is simply a psychiatrist helping a child who sees dead people — even if it’s a child hallucinating these haunting visions. The revelation that Dr. Malcolm Crowe was dead all along, however, changes not just the ending, but the entire movie. Lindelof told Vox in 2004 that the reaction is, “Oh, I didn’t even think I was sitting in that movie.” The twist makes The Sixth Sense “completely and totally transcendent.

This revelation doesn’t just help explain why Locke comes off as a bit strange. It suddenly forces viewers to reconsider every carefully framed flashback in every episode. It also establishes that the Island can literally perform miracles. The crash is an absolute tragedy that leaves everyone stranded and fighting for survival, but for Locke, it has given him a new life. When we learn the truth about his past, Lost transforms from a survival story into a spiritual mystery about destiny, magic, and faith.

articles.title: The Street Fighter Movie Makes a Mistake Mortal Kombat Already Learned From
articles.summary: Why are fighting game movies so scared of fighting tournaments? The Street Fighter movie is just the latest example.
body: Put on your gis and gloves, fighting fans, because Street Fighter is now in theaters. The latest attempt to adapt the venerated fighting game franchise for the big screen may not be getting off to the best start with critics, but fans of the series will likely go check it out for themselves. The film does have its positive aspects, such as the gorgeous 2D animation used for flashback sequences as well as plenty of easter eggs and fighting moves ripped right from the classic games. But as a whole, Street Fighter is too slapdash to be a fully satisfying cinematic experience, and one of the biggest reasons why is that the film doesn’t use the seemingly obvious way to structure itself.

body: In a statement shared on Twitter/X, the companies said they are aware the game "has fallen short of both your expectations and our own standards".

articles.title: Gameplay footage emerges of reportedly cancelled Assassin's Creed game Destiny
articles.summary: Footage of a reportedly cancelled Assassin's Creed game set in ancient China has emerged online, including stealth kills, the series' leap of faith, and a spinning umbrella weapon.
body: Called Assassin's Creed Destiny, it was reportedly being made for current platforms at Tencent -owned TiMi Studio Group, which also worked on mobile game Assassin's Creed Jade.

According to MP1st, the clips were taken from portfolios belonging to people who worked on it, and most come from a prototype built in February 2025. It's thought Destiny's setting was 206 BCE, nine years after Jade's 215 BCE.

The main mission has a female assassin heading into a sacred palace under siege from the army of the warlord Xiang Yu, in search of a mysterious artefact, and an early-stage boss encounter involving the warlord also appears.

Elsewhere, a male character uses parkour to dispatch enemies, while a temporary test area shows the player using an umbrella-style spinning weapon, with ink-brush ability icons and a health bar on screen.

articles.title: Surprising no-one, Wizards of the Coast 'doesn't intend to voluntarily recognize' union efforts for the second time this year
articles.summary: Per the United Wizards of the Coast Union (UWOTC-CWA) account on X, WoTC is acting in an entirely unsurprising manner: "Yesterday, Wizards informed us that it doesn’t intend to voluntarily recognize the D&D or Studio X units of our union ahead of a vote.
body: A union composed of employees from the Magic: The Gathering Arena team unionised back in June of this year, giving WoTC until May to formally recognise it. Obviously, it didn't.

Later in the same month, WoTC sent physical letters to members of the company encouraging them not to go through with it on the vote—and while WoTC did technically adhere to the The National Labor Relations Act, it did also not-so-subtly imply that its current benefits would be "on the bargaining table for both parties to negotiate". These letters were also allegedly accompanied by daily emails to employees.

Basically, it should not come as a surprise that Wizards isn't intending to recognize the full United Wizards of the Coast Union—a coalition now formed of members in both the D&D team and Studio X (Magic: The Gathering's creative staff)—either.

"We are best able to keep building great games and a great place to work by working directly with employees, not through unions. In this regard, Wizards is not neutral on the question of unionization … in the end, we will respect the results of the election, no matter what our employees choose."

articles.title: Discussion time: Do you think zone chats in MMOs are forces for good, or evil?
articles.summary: Terminally Online. This is Terminally Online: PC Gamer's very own MMO column. Every other week, I'll be sharing my thoughts on the genre, interviewing fellow MMO-heads like me, taking a deep-dive into mechanics we've all taken for granted, and, occasionally, bringing in guest writers to talk about…
body: Ah, zone chats in MMOs—trade and general chats, /shouts and /yells. Intended as a way to render the social glue that binds these videogames together, they are often instead a tableau for (and I say this somewhat affectionately) absolute lunacy, pock-marked with some of the most vile verbiage you'll see online.

Take, for instance, the time-honoured tradition of "Barrens Chat" in World of Warcraft. Combine a big zone that spans around 10-15 levels along with proximity to a major city, and you get a certain kind of verbal hooliganry that, in my journeys through WoW: Forever, I was actually pretty nostalgic for.

I mean, sure, the Chuck Norris jokes have gotten a smidge old. But while collecting Zhevra Hoofs, I would find myself possessed to ask Barrens Chat philosophical questions, and while I never received much in the way of wisdom, responses were always entertaining.

I'm not so fond of trade chat, though, which—at least on the horde side of things—has mostly been dominated by a bot by the name of Margrave Tyrael. Who, I kid you not, was literally sitting there for days spitting out the same automated messages, questioning why Blizzard was deleting beta characters.

articles.title: This game about grinding mute lumps of shapeless flesh has made me realise I've been hornswoggled by capitalism
articles.summary: Weird Weekend. Weird Weekend is our regular Saturday column where we celebrate PC gaming oddities: peculiar games, strange bits of trivia, forgotten history. Pop back every weekend to find out what Jeremy, Josh and Rick have become obsessed with this time, whether it's the canon height of Thief's…
body: I am a stakhanovite, a hero-worker. My productivity is not measured in grams but kilos. My working hours have been divided and subdivided into ultimate efficiency: not a nanosecond is wasted.

That is, in Flesh Grinding, whose demo I've been mucking about with. Not in real life, where my working hours consist mostly of staring at a blank Google Doc and wondering if I'm a moron who could never actually write at all.

Anyway, Flesh Grinding, which releases in Q4 2026—not to be confused with Fleshgrinder, which releases in Q1 2027; good luck—is a labour simulator. It's also one of those PS1-style horror games that are so fashionable right now. But mostly it is a game about working.

Working, specifically, with flesh—great, distended chunks of the stuff that plop down from the ceiling and amass in shiny piles. You must pick them up, walk them to your grinder, then turn them to mince. You must do this until your IV drip runs out of fluid, at which point it is time to return to your home and upgrade yourself, spending the millilitres of blood you scrounged from your grinding on upgrades.

articles.title: Ghostwire: Tokyo joins GOG Preservation Program, which means you don't have to deal with Bethesda.NET anymore
articles.summary: Ghostwire: Tokyo, Tango Gameworks' spooky, neon-drenched action-adventure game, is now officially a good old game. Granted, it's not that old, but 'good' seems about right given that contributing writer Imogen Mellor scored it a 72 in her review.
body: If you're wondering why a game from 2022 would need to be preserved already, well, it kind of doesn't. You may be thinking the game is finally free from its seemingly arbitrary implementation of Denuvo, but that was actually removed shortly after it was added. What this release does is remove Bethesda.NET integration (providing any extra goodies on your first launch of the game) and come with a promise from GOG that any stability issues that arise as decades pass and operating systems change will be addressed in future patches.

That may just come into play given that Tango Gameworks would be closed right now if Xbox's sudden closure of the studio hadn't been canceled out with an acquisition by PUBG owner Krafton. It's worth noting that the game still appears to be published by Bethesda Softworks, so if you're trying to avoid Microsoft products for any genocide-related reasons, you'll have to weigh that as a consideration.
